title: Write four more fractions equivalent to one half
description: Cutting each half of a strip into the same number of equal slices gives fractions of the same length as one half. Multiplying the numerator and the denominator by the same number gives four of them, while Keeko doubts it by adding one to both numbers.
teaching_notes: One idea: multiplying the numerator and the denominator by the same number gives an equivalent fraction. Watch for students who add the same number to the top and the bottom.

source: Find some more fractions equivalent to 1/2. Write four of th
video_script.why: The child writes four fractions equivalent to one half by multiplying the numerator and the denominator by the same number.
video_script.substitution: none: the book's own strip cut into halves and then into more equal slices
video_script.anchor: a paper strip cut into two equal halves with one half shaded
video_script.wrong_answer: add one to the top and the bottom
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says add one to the top and the bottom, so one half becomes two thirds. Two thirds of the same strip reaches past the middle, so adding one gives a different amount.
video_script.payoff_line: Four fractions equivalent to one half are four eighths, five tenths, six twelfths and seven fourteenths

final_answer.value: For example 4/8, 5/10, 6/12, 7/14 (any fraction whose denominator is twice its numerator).
final_answer.spoken: four eighths, five tenths, six twelfths and seven fourteenths

video_script.fraction_reading: one half, four eighths, five tenths, six twelfths, seven fourteenths
maths_rules: 1/2 is one of 2 equal halves of a strip
cut each half into the same number of equal slices: the shaded length does not change
multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number
any fraction whose denominator is twice its numerator is equivalent to 1/2
slip: Keeko adds 1 to the top and the bottom to get 2/3; 2/3 is more than 1/2
video_script.design: One idea: the same number multiplies both the numerator and the denominator. The strip stays on screen and each half is cut into more slices.

beats.on_screen: To find: four fractions equivalent to 1/2

beats.on_screen: Step 1: multiply the numerator and the denominator of 1/2 by the same number

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Step one, multiply the top and bottom numbers of one half by the same number.
Cutting every half into the same number of slices does exactly this.

marks.four: the strip shows each half cut into 4 slices, 4 of the 8 slices shaded
marks.five: each half is cut into 5 slices, 5 of the 10 slices shaded

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step two, multiply by four, because each half is cut into four slices. That gives four eighths.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Multiply by five to get five tenths.

marks.six: each half is cut into 6 slices, 6 of the 12 slices shaded
marks.seven: each half is cut into 7 slices, 7 of the 14 slices shaded

narration: <bookmark mark='six'/>Step three, multiply by six to get six twelfths.
<bookmark mark='seven'/>Multiply by seven to get seven fourteenths.

beats.on_screen: Answer: for example 4/8, 5/10, 6/12, 7/14 (any fraction whose denominator is twice its numerator).

marks.pay: the answer is written and boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>Four fractions equivalent to one half are four eighths, five tenths, six twelfths and seven fourteenths.
In each one, the bottom number is twice the top number.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: add 1 to the top and the bottom, 1/2 becomes 2/3; a strip of the same whole cut into thirds with 2 shaded sits under the half strip and reaches further; the bubble is struck out

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble about adding one appears
marks.longer: a strip cut into thirds with two shaded sits under the half strip and reaches past the middle

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks to add one to the top and the bottom, so one half becomes two thirds.
<bookmark mark='longer'/>But two thirds of the same strip reaches past the middle.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>Two thirds is more than one half, so adding one gives a different amount.
